country.paper_says: The study concerns India and the Indian government’s Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin).

study_design.paper_says: This was a qualitative interview study using framework analysis, but the paper states that the interviews “followed a structured format,” not that they were semi-structured.

population.paper_says: “I interviewed 17 people chosen to represent a range of types of SBM(G) actors operating at national, state and district levels.” Participants included civil servants, people assigned to SBM(G), partner-organisation employees and academics.

urban_rural.paper_says: The paper explicitly states: “The study also focused purely on sanitation programming aimed at households in rural India.” It was not a mixed urban–rural study.
urban_rural.where: p. 9, Strengths and weaknesses of the study

service_provider.paper_says: The study examines SBM(G) actors and sanitation administration at national, state and district levels, including the Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation and district officials.

regulatory_model.paper_says: The SBM(G) institutional framework included high-level political leadership, time-bound targets, monitoring through meetings, video conferences and a live dashboard, and holding district collectors accountable for results.
regulatory_model.where: pp. 3–5, Results—Interventions and Changes to the environment in districts; p. 8, Discussion

effect_measure.paper_says: The paper used qualitative framework analysis of interview transcripts, but describes the interviews as structured rather than semi-structured: “The interviews followed a structured format” and analysis used familiarisation, thematic framework identification, indexing, charting, mapping and interpretation.

effect_estimate.paper_says: The paper reports 17 interviews and official toilet-coverage growth from 39% to over 95% between 2014 and mid-2019. It supports political commitment, ambitious targets, real-time monitoring, accountability, communications, staffing, rewards and recognition as mechanisms. However, it does not specifically identify competitive district/state rankings, and it does not establish that prior programmes had similar technical and financial inputs.
effect_estimate.where: p. 1, Abstract; pp. 3–8, Results and Discussion—Principal findings

extraction_note.paper_says: The extraction note identifies the supplied record as RA0005AC70700; this is administrative metadata rather than a paper-reported characteristic.

parsed.overall_comment: Most descriptive fields are supported, but the paper calls the interviews structured rather than semi-structured, reports a sample of 17, and explicitly characterizes the study as rural-only. The effect-estimate summary also adds unsupported claims about competitive rankings and equivalent prior-programme inputs.
